text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Credit Foncier unions to meet today and call for a withdrawal of Finance Minister Jean Arthuis's restructuring plan after first encounter between unions and government-appointed mediator failed to defuse crisis.
-- Small and medium-sized firms created 40,000 new jobs in 1996, according to a bank study.
-- CDR structure selling off Credit Lyonnais assets sell stakes in Euris and Fonciere Euris.

-- Finance Ministry to freeze some 20 billion francs of budget credits, to offset a possible surge in government spending in 1997, a crucial year for the implementation of the Maastricht treaty criteria.

-- EU authorities will open investigation on planned further state help to French insurer GAN, EU commissioner Karel Van Miert says in an interview. Ha adds he expects to be presented with the government's plan for Credit Foncier before the end of January as agreed with the French government.
-- French ready-to-wear industry suffers from Italian and U.S. competition.
-- Banking group Credit National - BFCE to change name to Natexis.
-- Prime Minister puts an end to fixing wage ceilings for state-owned firms.
-- Unions start sixth day of occupation at the Paris headquarters of Credit Foncier de France.

-- Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet says in an interview that Europe needs "young people with bold ideas to foster new segments of our economy", adds he favours some extent of flexibility on labour markets, without trying to duplicate the American example, for fear of damaging Europe's social cohesion.
